newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's union boards to resign over press law.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's union boards to resign over press law.

text.p: Jordan's professional union board members will resign en masse within a month unless the government eases press restrictions imposed last week, doctors' union head Basim Dajani said on Thursday.

Dajani said the decision was taken on Wednesday night at a meeting of representatives of the 13 influential unions, which have tens of thousands of members and have often spearheaded opposition to the government.
Union heads have already announced they will resign on Saturday if the government does not rescind a controversial press law issued last week. The government has said it has no plans for concessions.
"All the executive councils of the professional unions will resign on June 21 unless the government withdraws the press law," Dajani told Reuters.
Board members of the journalists' union, who submitted and then withdrew their resignations earlier this week, will meet on June 6 to decide what further action to take, Dajani said.
The revised press law, the third law to be issued in a week by the government without recourse to parliament, set sweeping restrictions on reporting and stiffened fines for offenders.
It also imposed financial obligations on newspapers which journalists said would force most of Jordan's small but vocal opposition weekly papers to close.
"We feel this law was issued hurriedly, without consultation with us or parliament or with any of the concerned people," Dajani said. "We are cornered, unable to express our opinion."
Ten journalists were arrested and detained for eight hours on Tuesday at a protest over the new press law. Most said they were covering the demonstration, not participating in it.
The government has said it introduced the press law to ensure that "journalistic freedom will be a responsible freedom at the service of the country and its people".
